title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is currently navigating a mix of technological advancements and regulatory approvals, with notable movements in satellite development and defense tech collaborations. As companies vie for market share, the hiring landscape is becoming increasingly competitive, even as some legacy firms hesitate.

themes.title: Cubesats Gain Traction
themes.body: Parabilis is testing a propulsion system aimed at enhancing the maneuverability of cubesats, a sector that continues to attract attention for its potential applications. This could signal a shift in how smaller satellites are utilized in both commercial and defense contexts.

themes.title: FCC's Green Light for Reflect Orbital
themes.body: The FCC's approval of Reflect Orbital's satellite marks a significant step in the ongoing evolution of satellite technology, particularly in solar redirecting capabilities. This could pave the way for innovative applications in energy management and climate monitoring.

themes.title: Hiring Trends in Space Sector
themes.body: The space industry is grappling with the challenge of ambitious hiring plans against a backdrop of traditional corporate caution. This tension reflects a broader struggle to balance innovation with the realities of workforce management in a rapidly changing environment.

themes.title: Defense Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech sector is showing signs of life as the IPO window appears to be cracking open, prompting speculation about which companies might take the plunge. This development could reshape investment dynamics in an industry long dominated by established players.
